_about.note: Evidence category of every number and claim of the scout update (scout rover, ore deposits, broken-down rover, ASTRA-style HUD). Categories: balance (game tuning, no source; never a NASA figure), illustrative (story text shown in place of a measurement), unchecked (a public NASA page named here but NOT yet entered in docs/source_register.md; the claim must be checked before it is shown as a citation).

scout_speed_m_per_hour.note: 150 m per game hour, so a trip to the nearest site takes about one game hour. Chosen for pacing; the game does not claim it is a real rover speed.

scout_survey_hours.note: 0.5 game hours of looking around at a site before the report is radioed home.

scout_assemble_parts.note: 2 spare parts to finish the half-built scout.

scout_power.note: The scout is said to run on a radioisotope power unit, so it never needs charging, like NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers. The game does not model its power.

ore_per_deposit.note: 3 pieces of ore per deposit; each collect takes 1.

hematite_per_part.note: 2 hematite make 1 spare part at the workbench (simple cast iron brackets and frames). A game simplification: no smelter is modelled and no motor or electronics are made from rock.

science_per_ore.note: 1 science point per science ore studied at the workbench.

crew_rover_science_needed.note: 3 science points and Resources level 1 are shown as the goal for taking the crew rover out. The crew rover itself belongs to the rover update (Prompt 10).

SC1.note: NASA/JPL, Opportunity rover: hematite spherules ('blueberries') at Meridiani Planum. https://mars.nasa.gov/mer/ - to be entered in the source register.

SC2.note: NASA/JPL, Perseverance rover: olivine-rich rock on the floor of Jezero crater (Seitah). https://mars.nasa.gov/mars2020/ - to be entered in the source register.

SC3.note: NASA/JPL, Curiosity rover: calcium sulfate (gypsum/bassanite) veins at Gale crater, deposited by water. https://mars.nasa.gov/msl/ - to be entered in the source register.

SC4.note: NASA/JPL, Perseverance rover: carbonates at the margin of Jezero crater, a target in the search for signs of ancient life. https://mars.nasa.gov/mars2020/ - to be entered in the source register.
